=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 4 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The documented command `git merge --no-edit origin/<source>` does not set the documented [claude-asset-sync] merge subject.
  WHY: Following the procedure produces Git's default merge subject, which breaks the commit-prefix contract that downstream tooling greps for.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:253-258 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The shallow-history two-dot fallback uses git diff "${upstream}" HEAD, which reverses the intended comparison direction.
  WHY: It reports local branch-local guard edits as upstream staleness, which can trick an operator into merging branch-local changes.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:233-236 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When origin/HEAD cannot be resolved, the hook falls back to hardcoded main.
  WHY: In repositories where the default branch is not main, this fallback prevents the hook from detecting and reporting stale Claude assets.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:238-242 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fetch has no time bound when GNU timeout is unavailable.
  WHY: A slow network or proxy can hang the SessionStart hook indefinitely, delaying repository startup.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:238-242 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The hook fetches from origin on every SessionStart, including when the local checkout is already up-to-date with upstream.
  WHY: This adds unavoidable network latency to every startup, even when no drift is possible.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md, .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md, .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md, .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:Entire file diff | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: This PR modifies both the .claude/ and workflow-templates/.claude/ copies of the guard files, directly contradicting the stated Twin-first workflow requirement that only workflow-templates/.claude/** twins should change.
  WHY: Contradicts project conventions; risks divergence between templates and effective guards, and complicates the intended automated twin-sync process.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: "Only the `workflow-templates/.claude/**` twins change in this PR. The master session copies them into `.claude/` as a `[claude-twin-sync]` commit."
  expected_change_site: Only `workflow-templates/.claude/**` files should be modified in the PR diff
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The PR diff shows modifications to both `.claude/` and `workflow-templates/.claude/` files (`.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md`, `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md`, `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`, `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`, and their twins). While the last commit `c9c1620` is a `[claude-twin-sync]` that synced `implement-plan-claude.md`, the diff still shows both sides modified, indicating earlier commits modified both sides before the twin-sync. The PR description explicitly states the twin-first workflow, but the PR diff violates it. The progress log acknowledges this ("waiting for the master's `[claude-twin-sync]`") and the twin-parity tests are expected to fail until the sync completes, but the PR diff itself should not show modifications to both sides.
